title: How to open a new finder window in Finder on Mac: shortcut and menu steps
metaTitle: How to open a new finder window in Finder on Mac
description: How to open a new finder window in Finder on Mac: press ⌘N, use File > New Finder Window, or click the Dock icon first. Steps and fixes.
targetKeyword: how to open a new finder window in finder on mac
secondaryKeywords: open folder in new finder window
intro: Click the Finder icon in the Dock, then press ⌘N. That opens a new Finder window, and File > New Finder Window does the same thing from the menu bar.
tldr: Click the Finder icon in the Dock, then press ⌘N to open a new Finder window.
File > New Finder Window does the same job from the menu bar.
⌥⌘N creates a Smart Folder instead. ⌘T shows or hides the tab bar.
To open folders as tabs, change the settings in Finder > Settings > General and in Desktop & Dock.
Apple's guide is labeled macOS 27 Golden Gate, so check your version if your menus look different.

blocks.text: Finder is the app that shows your files, folders and drives on a Mac. Every Finder window shows one folder or location. You can have as many open as you need. This page covers the three routes in Apple's current guide, plus the settings that decide what a new window shows and whether it opens as a tab.
Open a new Finder window with Command N

This is the fastest route, and it is the one most people use. First, make Finder the active app. Click the Finder icon in the Dock. Apple's guide starts with that click. Then press Command N, written ⌘N. A new Finder window opens on your screen.

How do you know Finder is active? Look at the menu bar across the top of the screen. The word Finder sits just to the right of the Apple menu. When another app is active, that app's name appears there instead.

The click matters because keyboard shortcuts go to the active app. Community posts say ⌘N in another app runs that app's own New command, which may create a document instead. Apple's shortcut page does not confirm that detail, so test it on your Mac before you rely on it.
Open a new Finder window from the File menu

The File menu sits just to the right of the Finder menu in the menu bar. Click the Finder icon in the Dock first, so Finder is active. Then open File and choose New Finder Window. The result matches the shortcut.
Use the menu when you cannot remember the key. The menu item shows ⌘N beside its name, so you can read the shortcut as you go. That habit saves a trip to a help page the next time.
Count the actions. The keyboard route takes one click and one key press. The menu route takes three clicks. Pick the route that fits how your hands already work.

blocks.text: Apple uses ⌘ for Command, ⌥ for Option, ⌃ for Control, and ⇧ for Shift. Read ⌥⌘N as Option and Command pressed together, then N. Only ⌘N opens a plain Finder window.
Open folders as tabs instead of windows

Finder can open folders as tabs inside one window. Tabs help when you move between several folders. Two settings control this, and they live in different places. Check both before you decide which one you want.

items: Open Finder > Settings, then select General.
Tick Open folders in tabs instead of new windows to open folders as tabs.
Clear that box to keep separate windows.
Go to Apple menu > System Settings > Desktop & Dock, then find Prefer tabs when opening documents.
Choose Never to open folders in a new window, or Always to open them in a new tab.
Choose In Full Screen if you want tabs only in full-screen mode.

blocks.text: ⌘T is a third control. It shows or hides the tab bar when only one tab is open in the current window, as Apple describes it. Press it to show the bar. Press it again to hide the bar.
Choose the folder a new window opens to

The folder a new window shows comes from a setting. Go to Finder > Settings > General. Look for New Finder windows show. Apple describes it as the setting that chooses which folder displays when you open a new Finder window.

Apple's settings page does not list the options in that dropdown. Open it on your Mac and read what it offers. Do not copy a dropdown list from an article without checking your own Mac. For the full setup, read [how to change the default folder for new windows in Finder on Mac](/how-to/change-the-default-folder-for-new-windows-in-finder).
A worked example: two folders side by side
Say you are sorting invoices from Downloads into a client folder in Documents. Click the Finder icon in the Dock, then press ⌘N. Go to Downloads in the first window.
Press ⌘N again. Go to the client folder in the second window. Now you can move files between them without losing your place in either one.
Each window keeps its own location. If a new window opens on the wrong folder, return to New Finder windows show and check the setting. Then press ⌘N once more to test.
Option Command N opens a Smart Folder
Option Command N is easy to hit by mistake. It creates a new Smart Folder, which Apple's shortcut list gives as a separate action from a new Finder window.
If you wanted a plain window, press Command N without Option. Then check the window before you save or drag anything into it. A Smart Folder is a saved search, not a folder on disk.
When New Finder Window is missing from the menu

A community thread from November 21, 2025 describes a gap on macOS Tahoe 26.1. The Desktop right-click menu lacked Open in New Tab and Open in New Window. Replies suggested File > New Finder Window or ⌘N, then View > Show Toolbar.

No Apple staff replied in that thread. Treat the replies as workarounds from other users, not an official fix. If you see the same gap, use the File menu or the keyboard, and check the View menu for Show Toolbar.
Mistakes people make with new Finder windows

items: Pressing ⌘N while another app is active. Click the Finder icon in the Dock first.
Pressing Option too, which makes a Smart Folder instead of a window.
Changing New Finder windows show and expecting tabs. That setting picks the folder. The tab options are separate.
Changing one tab setting and missing the other one in Desktop & Dock.
Looking for Finder on iCloud.com. That site is a separate web interface, not a window in the Mac Finder.

blocks.text: Check your macOS version first

Apple's page for these steps is labeled macOS 27 Golden Gate. Its version selector lists macOS Tahoe 26, Sequoia 15 and older releases. The page does not say which steps apply to which version, so treat the steps above as Apple's current instructions.

To check your version, click the Apple menu and choose About This Mac. Write the version down before you follow an older guide. If a menu name on your Mac differs from the steps, match the closest one and test the shortcut first.
Finder on the Mac versus iCloud.com

Some people look for Finder in a browser. iCloud Drive can be reached at iCloud.com. Apple's setup page says that on a Mac you find iCloud Drive under Locations in the Finder. Apple does not compare the two, so use the Mac app when you need a new window.
Where to go next

Once the window is open, you will probably move around. [Go to a folder](/how-to/go-to-a-folder-in-finder) when you know the path. [Search for a file](/how-to/search-for-a-file-in-finder) when you do not. [Show the path bar](/how-to/show-the-path-bar-in-finder) to see where you are in the folder tree.

faq.question: What is the fastest way to open a new Finder window on a Mac?
faq.answer: Click the Finder icon in the Dock, then press Command N (⌘N). File > New Finder Window does the same thing. The keyboard is quicker once the habit sticks.

faq.question: Why does Command N not open a Finder window?
faq.answer: Finder is probably not the active app. Click the Finder icon in the Dock or the desktop, then try again. Community posts also report that ⌘N in another app runs that app's own New command. Apple's shortcut page does not confirm that, so test it on your Mac.

faq.question: Can Command N open a new tab instead of a window?
faq.answer: Not by itself. Tabs come from two settings. Finder > Settings > General has Open folders in tabs instead of new windows, and Desktop & Dock has Prefer tabs when opening documents. ⌘T shows or hides the tab bar.

faq.question: What does Option Command N do in Finder?
faq.answer: Option Command N creates a new Smart Folder. Apple's keyboard shortcut page lists it separately from the new Finder window. Use plain Command N when you want a normal window.

faq.question: How do I change the folder a new Finder window opens to?
faq.answer: Go to Finder > Settings > General and find New Finder windows show. Apple describes it as the setting that picks the folder shown when you open a new window. Apple's page does not list the dropdown choices, so read them on your Mac.

faq.question: Does this work on macOS Tahoe or Sequoia?
faq.answer: Apple's current guide is labeled macOS 27 Golden Gate. The version selector lists Tahoe 26, Sequoia 15 and older releases, but the page does not say which steps apply to each one. Check your version under Apple menu > About This Mac.

faq.question: Why is New Finder Window missing from the right-click menu?
faq.answer: A community thread from November 21, 2025 reports that the Desktop right-click menu lacked Open in New Tab and Open in New Window on macOS Tahoe 26.1. Replies suggest File > New Finder Window or ⌘N. No Apple staff replied in that thread.

faq.question: Can I open a Finder window on iCloud.com?
faq.answer: Not as a Finder window. iCloud Drive can be reached at iCloud.com, and Apple's setup page says Mac users find it under Locations in the Finder. Apple gives no feature comparison between the two.

task: Open a new Finder window on a Mac
appliesTo: Finder on macOS, steps from Apple's macOS 27 Golden Gate guide
requirements: A Mac with Finder. Apple's guide for these steps is labeled macOS 27 Golden Gate.
Finder must be the active app, so the word Finder appears next to the Apple menu.

steps.name: Click the Finder icon in the Dock
steps.text: Click the Finder icon in the Dock. Apple's guide starts here, and the click makes Finder the active app. Look for the word Finder next to the Apple menu.
steps.tip: If another app's name sits next to the Apple menu, click the desktop, then try again.

steps.name: Press Command N
steps.text: Press ⌘N. A new Finder window opens. This does the same job as the File menu item.
steps.tip: Hold Command, then tap N once.

steps.name: Or choose New Finder Window from the File menu
steps.text: Click File in the menu bar. Choose New Finder Window. The window opens at the folder your settings choose.
steps.tip: The shortcut appears beside the menu item, so use it as a reminder.

steps.name: Pick the folder for new windows
steps.text: Open Finder > Settings, then select General. Find New Finder windows show and open the dropdown. Choose the folder you want new windows to display.
steps.tip: Apple's page does not list the dropdown options, so read them on your Mac.

steps.name: Turn folder tabs on or off in Finder
steps.text: In the same pane, find Open folders in tabs instead of new windows. Tick the box to open folders as tabs. Clear it to keep separate windows.
steps.tip: After changing the box, press ⌘N to test the result.

steps.name: Check the tab setting in Desktop & Dock
steps.text: Scroll to Prefer tabs when opening documents. Pick Never for folders in new windows, Always for new tabs, or In Full Screen for tabs in full-screen mode.
steps.tip: If folders still open as tabs, check this setting as well as the Finder checkbox.

troubleshooting.problem: Command N does nothing or makes a document
troubleshooting.fix: Finder is probably not the active app. Click the Finder icon in the Dock, then press ⌘N again.

troubleshooting.problem: The new window opens as a tab
troubleshooting.fix: Clear Open folders in tabs instead of new windows in Finder > Settings > General. Then check Prefer tabs when opening documents in Desktop & Dock and set it to Never.

troubleshooting.problem: A Smart Folder opened instead of a window
troubleshooting.fix: You pressed Option too, which makes ⌥⌘N. Press ⌘N without Option.

troubleshooting.problem: New Finder Window is missing from the Desktop right-click menu on Tahoe 26.1
troubleshooting.fix: A community thread reports this gap from November 21, 2025. Use File > New Finder Window or ⌘N instead. Replies also suggest View > Show Toolbar, but Apple has not confirmed a fix in that thread.

troubleshooting.problem: The new window shows the wrong folder
troubleshooting.fix: Open Finder > Settings > General and change New Finder windows show. Apple's page does not list the options, so pick from what your Mac offers.

troubleshooting.problem: Your menus do not match these steps
troubleshooting.fix: Check the version under Apple menu > About This Mac. Apple's guide is labeled macOS 27 Golden Gate and does not say which steps apply to older releases.
